the methodology allows for the identification of cloud field elements from an all-sky camera network.
a novel methodology of georeferencing cloud elements is developed and validated for two cloud field cases.

the development of a novel methodology to measure and characterize cloud fields from all-sky cameras.
developing an innovative methodology to georeference cloud fields from a portable allsky camera stereo network.
the study of clouds from an all-sky imaging perspective.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methodology developed here is a promising tool for the study of cloud field dynamics.
this study demonstrates the feasibility of a portable all-ski stereo camera network to measure cloud base height, horizontal cloud field position, and velocity fields at a given altitude.
the methodology is promising and can be used to georeference cloud fields in the context of measurement campaign with a portable network of cameras.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the methodology presented is able to georeference clouds in an all-sky image with a horizontal accuracy of 10 m and a height uncertainty of 20 m for a cumulus cloud field and a horizontal accuracy of a few meters and a height uncertainty below 10 m for a stratocumulus cloud field.
the methodology is able to identify and geolocalize individual clouds in the cloud fields and to deduce the macroscopic characteristics of the cloud field.
the cloud field is georeferenced with an uncertainty of 0.3 km on the x-axis and 0.5 km on the y-axis, and a cloud base height uncertainty of 50 m.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed methodology is able to geolocalize individual cumulus clouds in the cloud fields with an uncertainty of 50 m in both horizontal coordinates, and to determine their velocity field with a 0.2 m s−1 uncertainty in horizontal velocity and 1.2° uncertainty in the cloud motion direction.
the cloud base height is retrieved with a mean uncertainty of 50 m and the velocity field with an uncertainty of 0.3 m s−1.
the proposed methodology can be used for cloud field characterization, and the results are in good agreement with those obtained with the ceilometer.
